newsitem.title: USA: Family of U.S. woman killed in bombing to sue Iran.
newsitem.headline: Family of U.S. woman killed in bombing to sue Iran.

text.p: A lawyer for the family of a New Jersey woman killed in a 1995 bus bombing in the Middle East said on Tuesday he plans to sue Iran for its alleged role in the attack and will seek $150 million in damages.

Attorney Steven Perles said the lawsuit would be filed in federal court on Wednesday in Washington, D.C., by the family of Alisa Flatow, who was killed when a suicide bomber struck an Israeli bus travelling through the Palestinian-run Gaza Strip.

He said the civil lawsuit will name as defendants the Iranian government, its top leaders, the Iranian ministry for information and security and other Iranian officials, charging that they should be held responsible for the attack.
Perles said the case will be filed under anti-terrorism laws signed by President Bill Clinton last year that allow U.S. citizens to bring suits for alleged state-sponsored terrorism.

He said the lawsuit was believed to be the first since the changes in the law. The law created a new exception to the general sovereign immunity that foreign governments enjoy, allowing lawsuits in cases of alleged terrorism.
Flatow, 20, who was studying at a Jerusalem seminary, and seven Israeli soldiers were killed in the attack by an Islamic extremist. Perles charged Iran was behind the bombing.

He said the lawsuit seeks $50 million in compensatory damages and $100 million in punitive damages. Any judgment for the family could be paid through frozen Iranian assets in the United States, he said.
Perles said the lawsuit was intended to "serve notice to the Iranians that if you target Americans, your life is going to be very difficult, and it will be costly for you."
